newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh security forces crush prison revolt.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh security forces crush prison revolt.

text.p: Security forces on Sunday crushed a prison revolt in southwestern Bangladesh, ending a week-long uprising by prisoners across the country, police said.
They said hundreds of security officers raided the prison in Jessore early on Sunday and rounded up mutineers. A curfew was briefly imposed during the raid, police said.

"The securitymen encountered resistance by prisoners armed with knives and iron rods. There was a brief fight in which several prisoners and few of our forces were injured," one police officer told Reuters by telephone.
The Jessore prisoners began their revolt on Monday, setting off unrest in three other prisons, including the high-security Dhaka central jail.
"The jail mutiny has ended with the fall of the Jessore jail," the police officer said.

The mutiny was triggered by the release of 90 prisoners under an amnesty marking the country's 25th independence anniversary on Monday. Prisoners, angered at being excluded from the amnesty, were demanding freedom while others sought better treatment and food.
